plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of their own bid (as long as they bid above it). Bidding my true value ($15) is the dominant strategy - it ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and I don't overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid.

This auction structure (pay the second-highest bid) is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since the price paid depends only on others' bids, not my own bid amount (as long as I'm not the second-highest), bidding exactly my value maximizes expected profit: I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, and pay only the second-highest bid, ensuring non-negative profit whenever I win.

Since the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid (equivalent to a second-price auction), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win, while bidding lower reduces my chances of winning without improving the price I'd pay. Bidding exactly $42 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay.
